question: If \(x=\dfrac{1-i\sqrt3}{2},\) where \(i=\sqrt{-1},\) then \(\dfrac{1}{x^2-x}\) is equal to:
solution:
Compute \(x^2-x\) before taking its reciprocal, using \(i^2=-1\). Squaring gives
\[
x^2=\frac{(1-i\sqrt3)^2}{4}
=\frac{1-2i\sqrt3-3}{4}
=\frac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
The imaginary parts cancel when we subtract \(x\):
\[
x^2-x
=\frac{-1-i\sqrt3-(1-i\sqrt3)}2
=-1.
\]
This denominator is nonzero, so \(\dfrac1{x^2-x}=-1\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
